To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radiation and drug sensitivities of clonal RIF-1 subpopulations are independent of both their ploidy and their metastatic capacity.

(1) no differences in radiation response were observed between diploid, tetra and octoploid clones of the RIF- 1 mouse sarcoma; (2) a wide variation in melphalan sensitivity was observed between RIF-1 subclones; and (3) diploid RIF clones were more sensitive than either tetraploids or octoploids to CCNU treatment.

the radiation response of RIF- 1 clones is not related to ploidy or metastatic capacity, that the response of RIF-l clones to in vitro drug treatment is not related to either ploidy or metastasis, and that the in vitro response of RIF-I clones to melphalan or CCNU treatment correlates with their in vivo responses.

the relationship between ploidy and metastasis and the response of clonal sublines to X-radiations and cytotoxic drugs.

the ploidy of RIF- 1 clones does not influence the response to either radiation, adriamycin or melphalan, but it does influence the response to CCNU.
ploidy and metastasis are independent of the in vitro and in vitro response of RIF- 1 clones to X-radiations, adriamycin, melphalan and to CCNU.
